Stated Claim / Post Context:
Russell Brand accuser claims then 30-year-old comic raped her when she was 16 as she opens up about 'abuse'

Mia, who is now married and has a daughter, alleged that Brand sent BBC-funded taxis to take her out of school and bring her to his flat for sex.

Actual Article Body:
By ELEANOR MANN

Published:  08:27 AEDT, 15 November 2026   |  Updated:  17:02 AEDT, 15 November 2026

A woman who says she was groomed by Russell Brand when she was 16 and he was 30 has become the first of the former comedian's accusers to waive her anonymity.

Mia Latter, now 37, was known until now only as 'Alice', but decided to reveal her identity to open up about the alleged abuse she suffered at Brand's hands when she was just a teenager.

Mia said she was speaking out to campaign for a staggered age of consent that would outlaw relationships between adults and under-18s. The current age of consent in the UK - 16 - was set in 1885.

Mia, who is now married and has a daughter, alleged that Brand sent BBC-funded taxis to take her out of school and bring her to his flat for sex.

During his trial, Brand's defence team had claimed that the women who spoke out in the 2023 Channel 4 Dispatches documentary, 'In Plain Sight', were actresses and even questioned whether some existed - though Mia herself appeared in it as a silhouette and was given the name 'Alice'.

Brand denied all the allegations of the original investigation in 2023. Mia spoke to the police after the documentary aired, but the CPS decided not to include her in the trial. Officers told her they wanted her to give evidence at a potential second trial.

Mia Latter (pictured) is the first of Russell Brand's accusers to waive her anonymity, claiming the comic abused her when he was 30 and she was 16

Brand is accused by Mia of oral rape. Mia said Brand sent cars to take her out of school and bring her to his house that were paid for by the BBC while he hosted a show on Radio 6

They met in 2006, when Brand, who worked for MTV and the BBC at the time, stopped Mia in Leicester Square after she had gone shopping at Topshop.

The comedian went through her shopping bags and picked out a dress, telling her she would wear it on their first date.

Mia told the Sunday Times: 'I thought that the second I said, 'I'm 16' he was going to block me.' But instead, Brand asked if she wanted to have dinner the next day.

She said that on their first date he met her outside Belsize Park tube station and took her hand, asked her to confirm she was 16 and then said: 'I don't give a f*** how old you are. I just need to know where I stand legally.'

It was Easter Sunday, a detail Mia said she remembered because Brand told her their meeting was 'what Jesus would've wanted'.
